hints: Think about whether each oxide is basic, amphoteric, or acidic, since only acids and amphoteric oxides react with a base like NaOH.
Remember that $\text{MgO}$ is a basic oxide from Group 2, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ in the middle of Period 3 is amphoteric.
Check what happens to the strongly acidic non-metal oxides on the right, they dissolve easily to form sodium salts, leaving only one oxide untouched.
walkthrough:
**Sort the oxides by acid-base character**

Think of Period 3 from left to right. Basic to amphoteric to acidic. $\text{MgO}$ is basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_2$ are acidic.

Rule to use:
$$\text{basic oxide reacts with acid only, acidic oxide reacts with base, amphoteric reacts with both}$$

**Test each type with NaOH**

Sodium hydroxide is a strong base, so it will dissolve anything that can act as an acid. That means acidic and amphoteric oxides dissolve, but a purely basic oxide does not.

Examples:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$$
$$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Pick the insoluble one**

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_2$ all react and dissolve to give soluble sodium salts. $\text{MgO}$ is basic only, so it has no reaction with NaOH and stays as an insoluble solid.

options.A: Correct. $\text{MgO}$ is a basic oxide. It reacts with acids to form salts but does not react with bases, so it is insoluble in aqueous NaOH and remains as a solid.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, so it reacts with both acids and bases. With NaOH it dissolves to form soluble sodium aluminate, $\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is a strongly acidic oxide. It reacts readily with NaOH to give soluble sodium phosphate: $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 12\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 4\text{Na}_3\text{PO}_4 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{SO}_2$ is an acidic oxide. It dissolves in NaOH to form soluble sodium sulfite or hydrogensulfite, so it does not stay insoluble.
